description: What the world affords an actor, what it costs, and the cheapest way from here to there (US-1 and US-4 of 122-traversal-and-travel). Each case carries the WHOLE input — the authored traversal_link/3 graph with its costs and requirements, every mode the actor is currently using, the runtime traversal_blocked/2 closures, what the host’s ITraversalProbe answered for each geometric link, the shared energy/3 meter, and the fully resolved TraversalTuning — so a harness in any language reproduces it with no defaults table, no world file and no KB. There is no position, no transform, no path and no frame anywhere in this file: core owns WHERE an actor may go and what it COSTS, and where they are this frame is the host’s entirely. `expected.affordances` is every authored link out of `from`, REFUSED ONES INCLUDED, sorted by (to, mode, id) — a UI greys the ford out and says why, and a corpus that saw only the survivors could not pin the refusal. The refusal is the FIRST that applies in TRAVERSAL_REFUSALS order (unreachable, blocked, mode, impassable, stamina, requires, forbidden), and that order is as much the contract as the refusals are; `requires` and `forbidden` never appear here because they are the rules layer’s and a pure function may not call a KB — an affordance that carries an authored goal is `available` AND `conditional`. `expected.best` is the cheapest available way to one destination; `expected.route` is uniform-cost search with a fully-specified tie-break (cost, then fewer legs, then the canonically-first destination, mode and link id), so reversing the link list must not move one byte. `expected.graphFacts` is the same graph in the 110 vocabulary, where traversal_link/3 is per LINK and traversal_cost/3 and traversal_requires/3 are per EDGE because neither fact takes a mode. Every cost is integer and floored. Regenerate with `npm run traversal-corpus`.

cases.name: the-mode-multiplier-is-the-whole-of-swimming-being-harder-than-walking
cases.note: THE case the module exists for. Two ways out of the camp, both authored, and what each takes out of the SHARED energy/3 meter is the link’s authored cost scaled by what the mode is worth: a 4 walked is 4, a 6 swum is 15. The boat link across the same edge is refused for `mode` and kept in the list anyway, because a UI wants to grey it out and say why. An implementation that charges the authored number and ignores the multiplier reproduces nothing else in this file.

cases.name: the-cheapest-way-across-the-ford-wins-and-it-is-the-boat
cases.note: The same edge, two authored links, and the actor can use both. The boat costs 1 and the swim costs 15 because the hull is doing the work, so `bestAffordance` takes the boat — and the published `traversal_cost/3` for the edge is 1 for the same reason, while the swim affordance still says 15. Cost is per LINK; the fact is per EDGE, because the fact takes no mode. A port that publishes one number per link makes core and can_traverse/3 disagree.

cases.name: an-authored-requirement-leaves-the-affordance-open-and-conditional
cases.note: The rope is a `traversal_requires/3` goal, which is authored PROLOG and cannot be evaluated by a pure function — so the swim resolves `available` AND `conditional`, meaning "nothing core knows refuses it, and something core cannot evaluate might". The goal is carried verbatim for the rules layer to rebind to the caller. It is keyed by the EDGE, so the boat link carries it too: §7 authors the rope once and means it either way.

cases.name: a-landslide-closes-the-pass-one-way-and-leaves-the-other-way-open
cases.note: `traversal_blocked/2` is DIRECTED, exactly as the link is. The closure is authored on riverside_camp → ford_path and the actor is standing at ford_path, where the way back is untouched. An implementation that symmetrises a closure strands the player on the wrong side of a landslide they walked past, and it passes the case below and fails this one.

cases.name: a-closed-link-is-refused-before-the-host-or-the-meter-is-consulted
cases.note: The same closure, from the other end. `blocked` is the first rung of TRAVERSAL_REFUSALS after `unreachable` because a landslide is not a matter of opinion — the actor has the mode, the geometry would have allowed it and the meter is full, and none of that is reached. The ORDER of the refusals is as much the contract as the refusals are.

cases.name: the-host-answered-that-the-gap-is-not-jumpable-from-here
cases.note: The ONE thing an engine is asked, and the only case in this file where a host appears: a gap the world marked `geometric`, and a probe that said no from where this actor is standing. The answer is a boolean keyed by link id — no arc, no distance, no navmesh — and core prices the link from `traversal_cost/3` either way, so a host cannot make a jump cheaper or open a door a norm closed.

cases.name: a-geometric-link-nobody-answered-for-is-passable
cases.note: The documented degradation, pinned rather than promised. The identical case with no `geometry` at all — a headless simulation, a turn-based world, this corpus — affords the jump. A host that supplies no probe must not have every jump in the world refused, which is the direction `ITrajectoryProbe` degrades in too.

cases.name: an-almost-empty-meter-refuses-the-swim-and-not-the-walk
cases.note: One meter, and it is 120’s. The actor has 5 left: the walk costs 4 and is still afforded, the swim costs 15 and is not. Both are in one case precisely so a port cannot pass by refusing everything once the meter is low — and there is no second resource anywhere in this file, because "sprinting drains stamina" and "power attacks drain stamina" being two numbers is exactly what one meter prevents.

cases.name: negative-every-authored-way-out-is-refused-and-not-one-is-filtered-away
cases.note: THE negative case, and the one that stops the corpus passing vacuously. The actor is standing at the camp, three links go out of it, and they have no mode at all — so all three are pinned, all three carry `mode`, nothing is available and there is no route. An implementation that returns only the usable ways produces an empty list here and passes every other case in this file; one that treats an authored link as an open one produces three available ways and fails only here.

cases.name: negative-a-place-with-nothing-authored-out-of-it-affords-nothing
cases.note: The other negative, and a genuinely different mechanism: the watchtower is a dead end, so there is no link to refuse and the list is empty rather than refused. `unreachable` is an absence and not a verdict — the route back to the camp is `null` for the same reason, because the graph is DIRECTED and nothing was authored the other way.

cases.name: the-cheapest-route-is-two-legs-long-and-the-one-leg-route-loses
cases.note: Uniform-cost search, not breadth-first. Swimming straight across costs 15; walking to the ford and jumping the gap costs 4 + 6 = 10, so the LONGER route wins and the pinned steps say which links it used. A port that stops at the fewest legs agrees on the destination and disagrees on the price, which is the drift a shared save file cannot survive.

cases.name: a-route-carries-the-authored-goal-of-every-leg-that-asks-one
cases.note: The route to the ridge can only go through the water, so it is `conditional` and the rope goal rides on the leg that asks it. A caller plans over a conditional route freely — affordability and permission are settled leg by leg as each is taken — which is why a route the actor is currently too tired for is still offered: a rested actor was never going to be told the ridge does not exist.

cases.name: the-route-search-is-bounded-and-a-bound-of-one-leg-finds-nothing
cases.note: A guard, not a rule. An unbounded search over an authored graph a creator got wrong is a hang, and the pack’s `reachable/3` is cycle-safe for exactly the same reason. The ridge is three legs away and `maxSteps: 1` finds no route — the honest answer, not a truncated one.

cases.name: a-world-where-the-cliffs-are-gentle-prices-the-same-graph-differently
cases.note: Not one number in this module is a compiled constant. The identical authored graph under a world whose `modeCost` makes a climb cheap and the water punishing: the climb is 5 instead of 15, the swim is 24 instead of 15, and the cheapest route to the ridge changes because of it. A game tunes this in `WorldIR.traversal`; a port that hardcoded core’s defaults reproduces every other case in this file and fails this one.
